chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman: Is it permissible for her to wear a silk garment while she is in Ihram? He (peace be upon him) said: No, and it is permissible for her to wear it when she is not in Ihram.

key_terms.أَبَانُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ: Aban ibn Uthman, a prominent narrator in Shia hadith collections
key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: Ritual consecration or state of sanctity for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ الْفَضْلِ: Ismail ibn al-Fadl, a narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: Can a woman wear silk clothes while in the state of Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific prohibition of silk for women during Ihram, distinguishing it from general permissibility. This ruling highlights the distinct sartorial restrictions imposed on women compared to men, emphasizing that the ban is tied to the state of consecration rather than the fabric itself. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the nuances of female attire in ritual pilgrimage within Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Sama’at from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ismail Bin Al Fazl who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the woman, ‘Is it correct for her that she wears silken clothes and she is in Ihraam?’ Heasws said: ‘No! And, for her is that she can wear in other than her Ihraam’.
en.sarwar: 8. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Isma‘il ibn al-Fadl who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman if she can use silk clothes in the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, but she can use them in times other than her being in the state of Ihram.’”
